text:
This looks like early 2010. Unemployment is 9.7%, the fed funds rate is about 0.12%, and the 12-month equity return of +49.8% reflects the rebound from the March 2009 low. That points to February 2010 or nearby.

Several details narrow it down:
- Equity 12m return of +49.8% fits a window ending in February 2010, since the S&P 500 returned roughly 53% from the February 2009 level.
- The 10-year yield at 3.64% fits February 2010 (about 3.6%).
- Unemployment was 9.7% in February 2010 (it was 9.7% in January and 9.9% in March).
- Core CPI at 1.48% is right for February 2010 (around 1.3%), and headline CPI at 2.66% matches (2.1% in February, 2.6% in January).
- Payrolls averaged -35k over the 3 months, which fits January or February 2010.
- The VIX at 20.1 fits end of February 2010 (19.5), and January was 24.6.
- US large-cap's 1-month return of +0.8% fits February 2010 (+3% for the S&P), but January was -3.6%, so it does not fit January. The 3m return of +0.3% fits February, since December 2009 was +1.9%, January was -3.6%, and February was +2.9%.

Headline CPI YoY of 2.66% is January 2010 (2.6%) and February was 2.1%, but the published value is lagged, so the end-of-February snapshot may still show January CPI. That is consistent with February 2010.
